summary.headline: Behari Lal Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR151.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR29.7 crore (19.6% margin) and high-value share at 60.4%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's first earnings call as a listed entity, following its IPO (INR301 crore issue, listed 19 August 2026). Revenue from operations grew 18% YoY to INR151.7 crore and PAT rose 24.5% to INR19.2 crore, though both EBITDA and PAT fell sequentially against Q4 FY26, which carried INR5.9 crore of one-off state incentives. Mix improved: high-value products (rolls, castings, specialty alloys) reached 60.4% of revenue and EBITDA per ton rose to about INR13,500. Management guided to about INR80 crore of FY27 capex, with Unit 3 (centrifugal/foundry for ICDP and HSS rolls) targeted to start in Q1 FY28, while defense revenue is expected to become meaningful from FY28.

financial_highlights.change: +20.6% YoY; +18.3% QoQ (from INR23.3 crore); margin +39 bps YoY
Q4 FY26 had INR7.25 crore, of which INR5.9 crore state incentives

segments.name: Alloy steel products (bars 6-230 mm, valve/tool/die steel)
segments.commentary: 47.7% of Q1 revenue (FY26 share ~46%); includes recently introduced valve, tool and die steel grades.

segments.name: Metal rolls
segments.commentary: 25.8% of Q1 revenue (FY26 ~26%); supplied to steel majors such as SAIL, JSW, Tata Steel and Vizag.

segments.name: Engineering castings (500 kg to 25 t single pieces)
segments.commentary: 19.8% of Q1 revenue (FY26 ~20%); demand from power sector, crusher OEMs; recent 22-23 t single-piece casting for a thermal power customer.

segments.name: Forging ingots and shafts
segments.commentary: 1.9% of Q1 revenue, down from 4.4%, as management deliberately shifts steel into finished high-value grades.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex target of about INR80 crore; INR5 crore spent in Q1 and INR75 crore planned over the next three quarters. Funding split: IPO proceeds plus internal accruals.
Unit 3 (foundry, centrifugal casting for ICDP/HSS rolls) targeted to commence in Q1 FY28; exact capex amount not yet disclosed pending exchange filing.
High-value product share targeted at about 70% in the near future (currently ~60%).
Operating EBITDA margin expected to grow 20-25% over the next two to three years per management; prior-year operating EBITDA margin cited as around 25%.
Inventory days to be held at 90-100 days as high-value mix grows.
Defense revenue expected to become meaningful from FY28; no quantified mix target given.
capex_capacity: Melting capacity is 1.5x FY24 levels; last melting addition was in FY24, and management plans a considerable melting addition next year with Unit 3.
Unit 3 shed under construction and most machinery ordered; centrifugal casting (vertical and horizontal) planned to make ICDP and HSS rolls; commencement targeted Q1 FY28.

IPO net proceeds of INR93 crore fresh capital: INR56 crore for equipment and civil work at both facilities, ~INR7 crore for rooftop solar, small debt repayment and ~INR19 crore general corporate purposes. Management said part of GCP was already used for working capital within 15 days of receipt.
Planned investments in CNC machining, shot blasting, painting, NDT, finish machining and a NABL-accredited lab to make castings ready-to-use.
Solar power project funded from internal accruals to lower power cost.
demand_pricing: High-value share rose from ~47% (two-three years ago) to 57% in FY26 and 60.4% in Q1 FY27; EBITDA per ton rose from ~INR9,100 (FY25) to ~INR11,500 (FY26) and INR13,457 in Q1.
Order book INR162 crore / 13,138 t at 30 June (over one quarter of revenue), skewed to high-value products.
Thermal power sector demand is rising; management cites customer visibility to 2035 and orders for CNC machines to support castings.
Defense: orders from Bharat Dynamics and Nuclear Power Corporation of India plus private suppliers to defense customers; prototype revenue started; long approval cycles.
Automotive share fell to 33% (from 38.7% in FY26) as low-margin commodity alloy bars for forging customers are being redirected; infrastructure rose to 26.4% from 20.7%.
Imports of ICDP and HSS rolls about 3.5 lakh tons in FY26 per management; management says it is the first domestic player to add capacity for these grades.
Management attributed the export decline to timing of casting shipments and order phasing, and said the trend is not changed.

qa_highlights.question: What will drive growth given capacity utilisation is already around 90-91%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth comes from doubling melting capacity every three to four years (last addition FY24) and shifting mix to high-value products, which rose from ~47% two to three years ago to 57% in FY26 and 60% in Q1; Unit 3 melting addition is planned next year.

qa_highlights.question: Unit 3 capacity, commissioning timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 3 is targeted to commence in Q1 FY28; shed is under construction and most machinery is ordered. Exact capex not disclosed pending exchange filing; total FY27 capex target is about INR80 crore across IPO proceeds, internal accruals and solar.

qa_highlights.question: What is the defence and aerospace opportunity and when will revenue start?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders have come from Bharat Dynamics, Nuclear Power Corporation of India and private suppliers; a small revenue stream has started in prototyping. Management expects good numbers from FY28, with no quantified mix target; approval cycles are long.

qa_highlights.question: Update on centrifugal casting and foundry expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 3 will be a foundry with vertical and horizontal centrifugal casting for ICDP and HSS rolls, targeted for production next year. Management also cited thermal power demand visibility to 2035 and a recent 22-23 ton single-piece casting.

qa_highlights.question: Do you have order book or inquiries for ICDP/HSS rolls, when does commercial production start, and what are the entry barriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said existing customers buying static metal rolls would be the buyers for ICDP/HSS rolls and trial orders could come from day one; it cited scrap access, existing heat treatment and machining, and 21-country export reach as barriers. No quantified order book for these grades was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR80 crore FY27 capex has been spent in Q1, and what is the post-expansion high-value mix and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: INR5 crore was spent in Q1 and INR75 crore is planned over the next three quarters. High-value share is targeted at around 70% in the near future, and operating EBITDA margin (cited as around 25% in prior years) is expected to grow 20-25% over two to three years.

risks_watch: Capacity constraint: utilisation is about 90.5% and no new melting capacity is added until Unit 3 (targeted Q1 FY28), so volume growth in FY27 relies on mix and pricing.
Unit 3 capex amount is undisclosed and the INR80 crore FY27 capex target depends on IPO proceeds and internal accruals; watch quarterly capex spend (INR5 crore in Q1 vs INR75 crore planned).
Defence revenue timing: long approval and prototype cycles; management gave no quantified mix target beyond 'good numbers' from FY28.
Working capital: cash conversion cycle rose to 94 days from 93 days; inventory days guided to 90-100 as high-value mix grows; net working capital absorbed about INR10 crore in Q1.
Exports fell to INR8.6 crore from INR11.5 crore YoY; management attributes this to shipment timing, and the trend needs to be confirmed next quarter.
Q1 earnings base lower than Q4 on reported basis because Q4 included INR5.9 crore of one-off state incentives; sequential comparisons remain noisy.
key_quotes: We did not chase tonnage. We moved the mix.
judge us on high-value share and EBITDA per ton.
We are conservative with the balance sheet because we intend to be here for the fifth.
Even if the revenue increases by 5% to 10%, the PAT margin and EBITDA, they will increase much more than the revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the high-value mix, ICDP/HSS roll opportunity and defence pipeline, but noticeably vague on specifics: Unit 3 capex and defence revenue size were left unquantified, deferred to future exchange filings.
